chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Al-Hakam ibn Miskeen, from Amr ibn Abi Nasr, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'The people of the valleys (or plains) are encroaching upon us, and among them are the Jews, the Christians, and the Magians, so do we give charity to them?' He said, 'Yes.'

key_terms.أَهْلَ السَّوَادِ: People of the valleys or plains, often referring to inhabitants of rural or specific geographic areas in Iraq
key_terms.يَقْتَحِمُونَ: They encroach, rush in, or overwhelm

ai.seo_question: Can we give charity to non-Muslims like Jews, Christians, and Magians according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates the practice of giving *sadaqah* to the *Ahl al-Sawad* (inhabitants of the valleys, often referring to non-Muslims in Iraq) who are encroaching upon Muslim lands, explicitly including Jews, Christians, and Magians. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly view that charity to non-Muslims is permissible not merely for proselytization, but as a means of fostering goodwill (*muwala*) and securing peace in mixed communities. The inclusion of Magians alongside People of the Book highlights the broader applicability of this ruling to other monotheistic or dhimmi communities in historical contexts.
